newsitem.title: USA: N.C. court rules to protect shared tobacco papers.
newsitem.headline: N.C. court rules to protect shared tobacco papers.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc said Thursday a North Carolina court granted a temporary restraining order that prevents Liggett Group Inc from disclosing documents owned jointly with the other four major U.S. tobacco companies.

The ruling was granted on behalf of Philip Morris, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, Lorillard Tobacco Co, a unit of Loews Corp, and Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc.

The court decision was granted amid swirling developments on the tobacco litigation front, including reports that Liggett, a unit of Brooke Group Ltd, would soon announce an expanded litigation settlement package.

Sources close to the situation told Reuters a press conference was scheduled for 1600 EST/2100 GMT in Washington to announce the settlement between Liggett and a group of state attorneys general who are suing the tobacco industry to recover billions of dollars in state funds spent treating smoking-related illnesses.
The documents at issue in the North Caroline court are notes and other papers owned by the Committee of Counsel, a panel of attorneys and company executives from the major U.S. tobacco firms.

According to various sources and published reports, Brooke Group Chairman Bennett LeBow was prepared to include these papers among documents he would hand over to plaintiffs' attorneys as part of his new settlement deal.
"There is a right way and a wrong way to pursue discovery in litigation. The attorneys general are proposing to take an inappropriate route," Philip Morris said in announcing the court ruling.
"We cannot allow them to proceed in an unchecked, reckless fashion to undermine long-settled principles that protect from disclosure materials covered by attorney-client privilege," the company said.
